title: One Writer at a Time
goal: Order the statements so the log prints "was 10;now 100!".
hints: Every order compiles - non-lexical lifetimes end the shared borrow at its last use. The TEST is the judge here.
"was 10" means the peek happens before any push. Then grow, then bang.
explanation: All six orders satisfy the borrow checker - the shared borrow in peek ends on its own line, so mutation afterwards is legal in any arrangement. But only peek → grow → bang produces "was 10;now 100!": reads and writes are a timeline, and the compiler only guarantees the timeline is SAFE, not that it is RIGHT. That last distinction is what the tests are for.
